16	// harnaas contributes a block to — the project's memory file and its
17	// version-control ignore file — are committed, hand-edited text, so the
18	// ordinary non-executable default.
19	const managedFilePerm fs.FileMode = 0o644
20	
21	// managedBlock is a marker-delimited region harnaas owns inside a file the team
22	// also writes.
23	//
24	// The two markers are whole lines. Matching a whole line rather than a prefix
25	// is what stops a marker quoted inside a fenced code block, or an indented one
26	// inside a list item, from being read as the start of harnaas's region — the
27	// same rule the frontmatter reader applies to its closing delimiter, and for
28	// the same reason: the file's author is allowed to write about harnaas.
29	//
30	// The comment syntax is a field rather than a constant because the two files
31	// that carry a block do not share one: a memory file is Markdown and takes an
32	// HTML comment, an ignore file takes a `#` line. Everything else about editing
33	// a block is identical, which is why there is one editor and not two.
34	type managedBlock struct {
35		// begin is the line that opens the region.
36		begin string
37	
38		// end is the line that closes it.
39		end string
40	}
41	
42	// htmlManagedBlock returns the block named name, delimited by HTML comments.
43	func htmlManagedBlock(name string) managedBlock {
44		return managedBlock{
45			begin: "<!-- harnaas:begin " + name + " -->",
46			end:   "<!-- harnaas:end " + name + " -->",
47		}
48	}

50	// blockSpan is where a managed block sits in a file's bytes: from the first
51	// byte of the begin marker's line to one past the newline that ends the end
52	// marker's line, so replacing the span replaces the whole region and nothing
53	// around it.
54	type blockSpan struct {
55		start int
56		end   int
57		found bool
58	}
59	
60	// locateManagedBlock finds b in content.
61	//
62	// A file with no block at all is not a failure — it is the ordinary case on a
63	// first install, and the state a removal converges on. What is a failure is a
64	// file whose markers do not pair up: harnaas would have to guess where its
65	// region ends, and every guess either swallows somebody's writing or leaves a
66	// marker behind that the next run reads differently again.
67	func locateManagedBlock(file string, content []byte, b managedBlock) (blockSpan, error) {
68		var span blockSpan
69		open := -1
70	
71		for offset := 0; offset < len(content); {
72			line, next := lineAt(content, offset)
73	
74			switch {
75			case matchesMarker(line, b.begin):
76				if open >= 0 || span.found {
77					return blockSpan{}, &managedBlockError{File: file, Reason: blockDuplicated, Marker: b.begin}
78				}
79				open = offset
80			case matchesMarker(line, b.end):
81				if open < 0 {
82					return blockSpan{}, &managedBlockError{File: file, Reason: blockUnopened, Marker: b.end}
83				}
84				span = blockSpan{start: open, end: next, found: true}
85				open = -1
86			}
87	
88			offset = next
89		}
90	
91		if open >= 0 {
92			return blockSpan{}, &managedBlockError{File: file, Reason: blockUnclosed, Marker: b.begin}
93		}
94	
95		return span, nil
96	}

111	// with CRLF endings and one an editor trimmed differently are both recognized.
112	// Leading whitespace is not: an indented marker is inside somebody's list or
113	// code block, not harnaas's.
114	func matchesMarker(line, marker string) bool {
115		return strings.TrimRight(line, " \t\r") == marker

118	// setManagedBlock returns content with b's body replaced by body, appending the
119	// whole block where content does not have one.

121	// Everything outside the markers is carried through byte for byte. Where the
122	// block is appended, the only addition to the previous content is the newline a
123	// file not ending in one needs before a marker can begin a line — and the block
124	// is appended with no blank line before it deliberately, so that removing it
125	// again restores the previous bytes exactly rather than leaving a blank line
126	// behind for the next install to append a second one after.
127	func setManagedBlock(file string, content []byte, b managedBlock, body []byte) ([]byte, error) {
128		span, err := locateManagedBlock(file, content, b)
129		if err != nil {
130			return nil, err
131		}
132	
133		rendered := renderManagedBlock(b, body)

135		if !span.found {

137				return rendered, nil
138			}
139			updated := make([]byte, 0, len(content)+len(rendered)+1)

142				updated = append(updated, '\n')
143			}
144			return append(updated, rendered...), nil
145		}
146	
147		updated := make([]byte, 0, span.start+len(rendered)+len(content)-span.end)
148		updated = append(updated, content[:span.start]...)
149		updated = append(updated, rendered...)
150		return append(updated, content[span.end:]...), nil
151	}

153	// removeManagedBlock returns content with b and both its markers gone.
154	//
155	// Content with no block comes back unchanged rather than as a failure: removal
156	// is what every run with nothing to contribute does, and most of those runs
157	// meet a file that never had a block.
158	func removeManagedBlock(file string, content []byte, b managedBlock) ([]byte, error) {
159		span, err := locateManagedBlock(file, content, b)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		if !span.found {
164			return content, nil
165		}
166	
167		updated := make([]byte, 0, len(content)-(span.end-span.start))
168		updated = append(updated, content[:span.start]...)
169		return append(updated, content[span.end:]...), nil
170	}
171	
172	// renderManagedBlock is the block as it appears in a file: the begin marker,
173	// the body, the end marker, each on its own line.
174	//
175	// A body not ending in a newline is given one, because the end marker has to
176	// begin a line for the next run to recognize it. An empty body produces the two
177	// markers with nothing between them, which is a block harnaas owns and has
178	// nothing to put in — distinct from no block at all, and reached only by a
179	// caller that asked for it.
180	func renderManagedBlock(b managedBlock, body []byte) []byte {
181		var out bytes.Buffer
182		out.WriteString(b.begin)
183		out.WriteByte('\n')
184		if len(body) > 0 {
185			out.Write(body)
186			if body[len(body)-1] != '\n' {
187				out.WriteByte('\n')
188			}
189		}
190		out.WriteString(b.end)
191		out.WriteByte('\n')
192		return out.Bytes()
193	}
194	
195	// writeManagedBlock puts body inside b's markers in the file named name under
196	// the project root, creating the file when it is absent.
197	//
198	// A run that would write the bytes already there writes nothing at all. The
199	// content is what matters, so an unchanged file with an unchanged modification
200	// time is the honest record of a run that changed nothing — and it keeps a
201	// re-run out of every file watcher the team has pointed at their memory file.
202	func writeManagedBlock(root, name string, b managedBlock, body []byte) error {
203		content, err := readManagedFile(root, name)
204		if err != nil {
205			return err
206		}
207	
208		updated, err := setManagedBlock(name, content, b, body)
209		if err != nil {
210			return err
211		}
212		if bytes.Equal(updated, content) {
213			return nil
214		}
215	
216		return writeManagedFile(root, name, updated)
217	}
218	
219	// dropManagedBlock removes b's block from the file named name under the project
220	// root.
221	//
222	// An absent file, and a file that never carried the block, are both nothing to
223	// do. The file is left in place even where the block was the whole of it: what
224	// harnaas owns is the region between its markers, and the empty file that
225	// remains is a file the team can delete in one keystroke, where a file harnaas
226	// deleted is content nobody can get back from the manifest.
227	func dropManagedBlock(root, name string, b managedBlock) error {
228		content, err := readManagedFile(root, name)
229		if err != nil {
230			return err
231		}
232	
233		updated, err := removeManagedBlock(name, content, b)
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if bytes.Equal(updated, content) {
238			return nil
239		}
240	
241		return writeManagedFile(root, name, updated)
242	}
243	
244	// readManagedFile reads the file, reporting an absent one as empty content.
245	//
246	// "Not there yet" is the first-install case for every file that carries a
247	// block, and treating it as empty is what makes creating one the same code path
248	// as editing one.
249	func readManagedFile(root, name string) ([]byte, error) {
250		content, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name))
251		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
252			return nil, nil
253		}
254		if err != nil {
255			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", name, err)
256		}
257		return content, nil
258	}
259	
260	// writeManagedFile replaces the file's contents atomically.
261	//
262	// The write goes through jsonutil despite the package name and the file being
263	// Markdown or an ignore list: WriteFileAtomic takes arbitrary bytes and is the
264	// module's one atomic writer, and a second implementation would be a second
265	// place the stage-sync-rename sequence has to stay correct.
266	func writeManagedFile(root, name string, content []byte) error {
267		if err := jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic(filepath.Join(root, name), content, managedFilePerm); err != nil {
268			return fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", name, err)
269		}
270		return nil
271	}

273	// blockMarkerReason is why harnaas will not edit a file's managed block.
274	type blockMarkerReason string
275	
276	const (
277		// blockUnclosed is an opening marker with no closing one after it.
278		blockUnclosed blockMarkerReason = "unclosed"
279	
280		// blockUnopened is a closing marker with no opening one before it.
281		blockUnopened blockMarkerReason = "unopened"
282	
283		// blockDuplicated is a second opening marker in one file.
284		blockDuplicated blockMarkerReason = "duplicated"
285	)
286	
287	// managedBlockError refuses to edit a file whose markers do not pair up.
288	//
289	// The three reasons are one type because the reader's next action is the same
290	// in all three — open the file and look at the marker lines — and the message
291	// says which of them is there. What harnaas will not do is repair the markers
292	// itself: every repair is a guess about where the region the team can edit
293	// begins, and a wrong guess overwrites their writing with a block.
294	type managedBlockError struct {
295		// File is the file, named the way the reader sees it: relative to the
296		// project root.
297		File string
298	
299		// Reason is which of the three shapes the markers are in.
300		Reason blockMarkerReason
301	
302		// Marker is the marker line the reason is about.
303		Marker string
304	}
305	
306	func (e *managedBlockError) Error() string {
307		var problem string
308		switch e.Reason {
309		case blockUnclosed:
310			problem = fmt.Sprintf("%s opens a harnaas managed block with %s and never closes it", e.File, e.Marker)
311		case blockUnopened:
312			problem = fmt.Sprintf("%s closes a harnaas managed block with %s that was never opened", e.File, e.Marker)
313		case blockDuplicated:
314			problem = fmt.Sprintf("%s opens a harnaas managed block with %s more than once", e.File, e.Marker)
315		}
316	
317		return problem + "\n\n" +
318			fmt.Sprintf("Edit %s so the block appears once, opened and closed by its own marker line, "+
319				"or delete the marker lines entirely and re-run to have harnaas write the block again.", e.File)
320	}

19	const memoryFileName = "AGENTS.md"
20	
21	// instructionBlock is the region harnaas owns inside the memory file.
22	//
23	// The name in the markers is `instructions` rather than a bare `harnaas`,
24	// because the ignore file's block is harnaas's too and a reader meeting one
25	// marker should not have to know which of harnaas's blocks it delimits.
26	var instructionBlock = htmlManagedBlock("instructions")
27	
28	// instruction is one instruction asset's contribution to the memory file.
29	//
30	// It carries the source alongside the content because the block is committed:
31	// a reader opening `AGENTS.md` months later meets text nobody on the team
32	// wrote, and the comment above it is the only thing in the file that says where
33	// it came from.
34	type instruction struct {
35		// ID is the asset's id, which is what the block is ordered by.
36		ID string
37	
38		// Source is the asset's source spelled the way the manifest declares it.
39		Source string
40	
41		// Content is the asset's bytes, inlined verbatim.
42		Content []byte
43	}
44	
45	// renderInstructionBlock is the body of the memory file's managed block.
46	//
47	// The ordering is by asset id and not by manifest position, so moving an entry
48	// in `harnaas.json` regenerates a byte-identical block: the manifest's order
49	// says nothing about what the assets mean, and a diff that moved a thousand
50	// lines because somebody sorted their manifest would be a diff nobody reads.
51	//
52	// Content is inlined verbatim. The one byte that may be added is a newline
53	// after content that does not end in one, because the next asset's comment has
54	// to begin a line — every other byte of every asset arrives in the file exactly
55	// as it resolved.
56	func renderInstructionBlock(instructions []instruction) []byte {
57		ordered := slices.Clone(instructions)
58		slices.SortStableFunc(ordered, func(a, b instruction) int {
59			return cmp.Compare(a.ID, b.ID)
60		})
61	
62		var body bytes.Buffer
63		for i, entry := range ordered {
64			if i > 0 {
65				body.WriteByte('\n')
66			}
67			fmt.Fprintf(&body, "<!-- harnaas instruction %q from %s -->\n", entry.ID, entry.Source)
68			body.Write(entry.Content)
69			if len(entry.Content) > 0 && entry.Content[len(entry.Content)-1] != '\n' {
70				body.WriteByte('\n')
71			}
72		}
73	
74		return body.Bytes()
75	}

78	// these instruction assets, and removes the block when there are none.
79	//
80	// The empty case is a removal rather than an empty block on purpose: a block
81	// with nothing in it is a claim that harnaas has something to say here, and the
82	// state after the last instruction asset goes is that it does not.
83	func writeInstructionBlock(root string, instructions []instruction) error {
84		if len(instructions) == 0 {
85			return dropManagedBlock(root, memoryFileName, instructionBlock)
86		}
87		return writeManagedBlock(root, memoryFileName, instructionBlock, renderInstructionBlock(instructions))
